title: How and which AI are good to teach you some engine?
author: fairerman
selftext: I wanna make a simple tactical rpg on Godot, because far I know it's the easiest engine to run, but still got the fear and feel lost when I open it. For anyone that have using an AI tool to learn an game engine, it indeed taught you? And which one did you used?

comments.author: BugaiGames
comments.body: Claude can handle Godot very well without you learning it. If you have limited time better focus on architecture, game design,  UX and actually AI directing skills, while letting AI to handle codding . Right now all AI focused on codding so they pretty good in it, while lacking everything else

replies.author: fairerman
replies.body: I was messing around with Gemini pro, it was a fun experience cuz he made the game in html and java I think, all I had to do was type "I want the game to be like this and this". I kinda wanna learn how to code as well because I need something to work home office (I have a daughter now and need to expend more time with her). I'll be honest that I'm still a bit lost on what you say on architecture. Not planning launch the game for selling or anything like that, all art will also be AI (Midjourney, don't need sprites or animation thing). I just want to create a game that I would have fun playing with.

replies.author: BugaiGames
replies.body:
AI art is also separate skill, dont underestimate amoint of effort to get production grade assets even using AI.
PoC with ai fast, but than it slow down a lot. Try to focus on simplest possible version without anything extra and polish it to something you can present to a friend to play. That would be huge lesson to understand scale and effort. And past that it will be even slower.

Ps I failed and got scope creep in my game, and now stuck polishing and balancing all those mechanics and assets. And I have a lot of different experience in background

replies.author: fairerman
replies.body: The art will be like "TCG art": still image with some contour. The characters like a coin there with the image and the circle around it. But my concern is more learning the tool to eventually don't need the AI anymore.

replies.author: Dazzling-Try-7499
replies.body: Check out tutorials point. Also code project. One cool thing about ai though, you can ask it to teach you a language and even quiz you or critique your code and explain your mistakes.

replies.author: BertJohn
replies.body:
AI Doesn't lack everywhere else. Currently ChatGPT wired 92 animation transition states into 150\~ animations and hooked up an entire animator with complex states (0 through 7) with speed modifiers and multiple state conditions, And about 30 triggers to enter an animation.

  
The biggest limitation is the engine not being accessible for the AI, Unity's Latest MCP bridge concepts (Store version or unity's version doesn't matter) has brought AI FULLY to the front and it can test features like implementing multiplayer on a client, and then finding the edge case that the client if also the server needs its own handle case aswell. The hardest part is tokens being wasted in an MCP bridge that goes offline randomly.

comments.author: sharkymcstevenson2
comments.body: We're trying to solve this at tesana (www.tesana.ai), happy to give you some credits if you want to try it out!

comments.author: webdev-dreamer
comments.body: Posts like these make me happy that there is still some skill required even with AI

comments.author: Efficient-Pop-302
comments.body:
I didn't use AI to learn Godot, it was too unreliable and would more often than not provide me incorrect information.


Your best bet is to follow channels like GD Quest and read documentation as you build your projects. It'll help reinforce your learning and critical thinking skills.


If you become too reliant on AI for answers, you will never learn anything.

comments.author: Mauseleum
comments.body: Making a 2D xcom game atm. Claude code on desktop app. The game is nicely on the way that MVP is done. Huge amount of learning with architechting stuff but Claude teaches well and gives good structure for project imho. Its mostly going through .md s with claude and then claude does the work really well when the objective is clear. Now im so in so deep i took got with claude to project, but mostly for game sprite generation. I have a bad history with codex, but suppose i can use codex too if i run out of opus. OP, just start it ll all be learning and good

comments.author: Designer_Spell_7270
comments.body:
AI can totally help but use it more like a tutor. For Godot, it’s pretty good for stuff like signals, scenes, UI, and fixing small GDScript problems when you get stuck.

the best kind is the one that explains clearly and gives examples instead of dumping a huge wall of code. chatgpt is solid for that but some like Claude or Cursor. if you want something more godot specific, ziva sh  might be worth a look since it's made for godot and feels a bit more on point than a generic ai.
